headline: Anthropic Fellows report coordination failures in multi-user agent teams sharing resources
summary: An Anthropic Fellows paper studies agents acting for different users who share budgets, calendars, orders or software workflows. Across four simulated environments and 77 scenarios, the authors report that a single coordinator achieved better group outcomes than separate user agents in every environment. They evaluated up to five models, with model coverage varying by environment; the paper describes 20 episodes per scenario by default, with exceptions. The study identifies stalling as teams grow, overriding other users’ actions and unsupported claims, and reports setting-specific mitigations. Results are author-reported simulations, not independent replication or real-world deployment evidence.
